wiki.title: Nuln
wiki.description: Nuln, called the " Bastion of the South " and the " Jewel of the Empire ", is the capital city of the Electoral Province of Wissenland, the second largest city of the Empire of Man and the largest manufacturer and exporter of Imperial blackpowder munitions and warmachines, earning itself the title of the " Armoury of the Empire ". Sitting at the heart of the Old World 's southern trade routes, it stands as an imposing bastion, its fortified walls bristling with enough heavy blackpowder artillery emplacements to arm a fleet of war galleons.

wiki.title: Wissenburg
wiki.description: Wissenburg is a city and the capital of the Grand County of Wissenland in the Empire. Countess Emmanuelle seldom visits the city as she has only contempt for what she terms po-faced burghers and is actively seeking to seperate her beloved Nuln from Wissenland, keeping her own Electorial status and granting the Topenheimer family of Pfeildorf a new one for Wissenland.

wiki.title: Pfeildorf
wiki.description: Pfeildorf is an Imperial town and the former capital of the Grand Barony of Solland when it was still an Electoral Province before it was integrated into Wissenland following the Turmoil of 2512 IC. It is the centre of the Sudenland wool trade.

wiki.title: Ambosstein
wiki.description: Ambosstein is an empire village in Wissenland with a population of 80 people. 1

wiki.title: Steingart
wiki.description: Once the second city of Solland, Steingart is today a quiet agricultural market and a centre for the wool trade in eastern Wissenland. Ruled by Baron Frederich Hebart, Steingart would be on few maps were it not for the presence of extensive ruins to the southwest. These consist of a vast circle of standing stones, with a smaller ring of megaliths inside it.

wiki.title: Meissen
wiki.description: Meissen, the biggest port on the middle River Söll and the terminus of the trade road from the Dwarf hold of Karak Norn, is a bustling, prosperous Imperial town in Wissenland. Meissen is famed for its works in silver, and its goblets, tableware, and jewellery are in high demand over much of the Old World.

wiki.title: Hendorf
wiki.description: Hendorf is a Wissenlander town now known for its Myrmidian worship, it's located not far from the Grey Mountains.

wiki.title: Kreutzhofen
wiki.description: Far off in Sudenland’s west, deep in the foothills where the Vaults and the Grey Mountains meet, the village of Kreutzhofen serves as an important way station for trade with Bretonnia and Tilea, due to two key geographical features.

wiki.title: Kroppenleben
wiki.description: Situated far up the River Hornberg in the foothills of the Black Mountains, Kroppenleben is both a centre for the fur trade and the nearest sizeable market to the Dwarf realm of Karak Hirn. Ruled by the hypochondriac Baron Johann von Kalb, the village has a large population of Dwarfs for its size. The Dwarfs here act as guides or scouts for parties entering the mountains, and as brokers for traders coming to buy pelts brought in by trappers.

properties.name: Mecklenburg
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Kotzenheim
wiki.description: Kotzenheim was an empire village in Wissenland, with a population of 61 people. 2 Other sources place it in Averland.

properties.name: Öschel
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

properties.name: Lasperg
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Dotternbach
wiki.description: Dotternbach is an Imperial village located upriver from the Wissenland provincial capital of Wissenburg along the River Weiss, past Weningen. Formerly unremarkable save for a fine wool produced by local shepherds and the thriving wool trade that resulted, Dotternbach became famous when a team from the University of Nuln found pre- Sigmar cairns and tombs in overgrown gorges deep in the foothills. The news inspired a rush of treasure-seekers, and claim-jumping has become a problem.

wiki.title: Furtzhausen
wiki.description: Furtzhausen is an empire village in Wissenland, with a population of 74 people. 2 Other sources place it in Stirland. 1

wiki.title: Talagaad
wiki.description: Talagaad, the adjacent town that serves as Talabheim 's port from outside the city-state's crater on the River Talabec. Talagaad, also spelled Taalagad or Talagad, is perhaps the largest and most important settlement claimed by the city-state of Talabheim in Talabecland. It is, in effect, Talabheim's port, and all river trade to the city-state passes through Talagaad's docks.

properties.name: Dankerood
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Terror in Talabheim

properties.name: Taggenfeld
properties.source: Warhammer: The Old World Roleplaying Game

properties.name: Flusgard
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Battles 6th Edition: The Nemesis Crown

wiki.title: Küsel
wiki.description: A day's journey upriver from the city-state of Talabheim is the town of Küsel, the provincial capital of Talabecland during the final years of the period of Imperial history known as the Anarchy in 2276 IC. It is a bustling port, with great amounts of lumber and fish regularly passing its docks.

properties.name: Egondorf
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Battles 6th Edition: The Nemesis Crown

wiki.title: Bek
wiki.description: Chief town of the province ruled by Count Josef von Behring, Bek is normally a quiet trading town that exports lumber from the Great Forest and dried fish, and collects tolls for the use of its quays. Since the war began, the town and surrounding area has been flooded with over a thousand refugees from Ostland, so many that they outnumber the townsfolk themselves. This has greatly strained resources and fights between locals and refugees are common and increasing in size.

properties.name: Nadjagard
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Battles 6th Edition: The Nemesis Crown

wiki.title: Hermsdorf
wiki.description: The southernmost settlement on the Old Forest Road is a small logging town with nearly 400 inhabitants. Hermsdorf is built near the crest of a low hill, overlooking the Wurtbad valley that extends 15 miles to the south. The local ruler, Baron Waldemar von Züten, spends most of his time carousing in Wurtbad and leaves routine administrative duties to his bailiff.

wiki.title: Priestlicheim
wiki.description: Priestlicheim is an Imperial settlement in Talabecland that is home to a large Sigmarite monastery, the Temple of Leopold the Hammer of Faith, separated from the Barren Hills by a stretch of the Great Forest. The Sigmarite brothers here are dedicated to the study and eventual eradication of whatever curses the Barren Hills.

wiki.title: Lieske
wiki.description: Site of the largest fortified coaching inn in Talabecland outside of Talabheim itself, Lieske is also the unofficial southern headquarters for a large contingent of roadwardens, who patrol from Talabheim to the Stir to keep the Old Forest Road safe. The inn, the "Taal's Bowers," has a half-dozen jail cells in its barn and a gallows in the yard, allowing justice to be effected on the spot. The roadwarden captain, Jörg Schmidt, will hold trials in the common room, drafting inn guests as jurors, if need be.

properties.name: Krieglitz
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

properties.name: Silberwald
properties.source: Warhammer: The Old World Roleplaying Game

wiki.title: Silberwald
wiki.description: Silberwald is a small town in Stirland. During the Skaven Wars after 1111 IC, it was the site of the infamous Battle of the Fellwald. Silberwald had been mostly spared the Black Death and Skaven attacks, but hordes of refugees overwhelmed the town's resources as thousands fled from the Undead attacks in Sylvania of the necromancer Frederick van Hal in 1122 IC.

properties.name: Eastadt
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Terror in Talabheim

wiki.title: Talabheim
wiki.description: Talabheim, known in ancient times as Taalaheim which means "Taal's Victory", is an Imperial city-state and the capital city of the Grand Duchy of Talabecland. It is one of the great cities of the Empire of Man and is the largest city in the eastern Empire. Talabheim lies deep within the Great Forest of the Empire, and as such earned its nickname as the " Eye of the Forest ", for like the eye of a mighty storm, the city is built within a great, shallow crater deep in the forest, an island of calm amidst the surrounding danger.

properties.name: Giehselhoff
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Maylhof
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Königstein
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Flensburg
wiki.description: Flensburg is a small market town in western Stirland. Located west of the Sirhügel Hills, the town's economy is based on the sheep trade from that region. The town also has a major temple of Shallya.

properties.name: Mittlenburg
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Sternieste
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Svar Mare
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Wurtbad
wiki.description: Wurtbad is an Imperial city and the capital of the Grand Province of Stirland that rests at the terminus of the Old Dwarf Road, surrounded by the Great Forest. By far the largest town in Stirland, its whitewashed walls and buildings and its busy docks and markets tell of a prosperous trading town. By decree of the Elector Counts, all the wine produced in western Stirland must be sold through Wurtbad, earning the town the sobriquet of "the wine capital of the Empire ".

properties.name: Bylorhof
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Bylorhof
wiki.description: Bylorhof is home to the worship of Bylorak, God of the Marshes, believed by some scholars to be an aspect of Taal or Manann. To the residents of this settlement, though, Bylorak is no scholar's aspect—he's their God, and they're proud to be his holiest site. When Vlad von Carstein began to drive the priests out of Sylvania, Bylorhof's priests of Sigmar, Shallya, and Morr all fled, but not the priest of Bylorak.

properties.name: Aulen
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Schramleben
wiki.description: Schramleben is a small town in Stirland in the Empire. It lies on the trade route from Stirland to the Dwarf Hold of Zhufbar. Even the Dwarfs of Zhufbar avoid Sylvania, preferring the road south to Schramleben and then through the Moot if they wish to travel to Wurtbad.

wiki.title: Vanhaldenhof
wiki.description: The Sylvanian village of Vanhaldenhof guards the road leading to the ruins of Vanhaldenschlosse.

properties.name: Helfurt
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Eschen
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Drakenhof
wiki.description: Castle Drakenhof was the former capital of the Imperial province of Sylvania during the reign of its last Imperial noble, Count Otto von Drak. Nearly all the rulers of Sylvania, living and Undead alike, have made the castle their seat of power. This accursed citadel was where Vlad von Carstein began his reign of terror, and from which battlements he summoned his Undead army.

wiki.title: Siegfriedhof
wiki.description: Siegfriedhof lies on the borderlands with the County of Sylvania near Hunger Wood. It is also the site of the Morrian Abbey of Blessed Aethelbert the Vigilant. Situated on the river near the Hunger Wood, Siegfriedhof is a small town owned by the Order of the Raven Knights, Morrian Templars dedicated to the destruction of the Undead.

properties.name: Zherden
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.name: Wartenhof
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Wartenhof
wiki.description: Wartenhof was a medium-sized Imperial town in Sylvania whose population was slaughtered during the Skaven Wars of the early 12th century IC. The town was large, having an impressive garrison and many buildings. The combination of an assault by the Black Death, the Undead commanded by the necromancer Frederick van Hal, and the Skaven of Clan Fester resulted in the town's people being entirely exterminated.

wiki.title: Waldenhof
wiki.description: Waldenhof, the capital town of the province of Sylvania in the Empire, is a walled town that sits where its tributary rivers come down from the mountains and merge together to form the River Stir.

wiki.title: Wörden
wiki.description: Found at the crossroads of the Old Dwarf and Moot Roads, the small town of Wördern lies within the Imperial Province of Stirland. The town has an approximate population of 1800 and is relatively poor, with dilapidated walls and ill-equipped guards. In addition, residents of Wördern are known to be particularly distrustful of outsiders.

wiki.title: Leicheberg
wiki.description: At the edge of the Haunted Hills by the source of the Black Run River, Leicheberg lives in fear of its neighbour to the east, Sylvania. Its ruler, Count Petr von Stolpe, has faced the Walking Dead many times in his life and is convinced the von Carsteins mean to expand beyond their ancient borders. He has argued many times at the court in Wurtbad for a campaign to cleanse Sylvania, but to no effect.

wiki.title: Marburg
wiki.description: Marburg has stood as a settlement of the Empire since the reign of Emperor Sigmar, but is at present only a small village in Stirland. The village is located in the thick forests just south of the River Stir, along a road between Wurtbad and Siegfriedhof. Due to its proximity to these forests, Marburg is regularly threatened by raiders such as Forest Goblins.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Vorchdorf
wiki.description: Vorchdorf is a village located in southeastern Stirland, near The Moot. Because of this, the town is populated by both humans and Halflings. The town is protected by a battered wooden palisade.

properties.name: Lichenheim
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Night's Dark Masters

wiki.title: Grünburg
wiki.description: Grünburg, sometimes spelled Grünberg is a town within the province of Reikland that supports a ferry system. Downriver from several major trading towns, Grünburg is no stranger to trade goods bound for the Reik, but it is in riverboat manufacture that Grünburg truly excels. The town’s boatyards are in constant operation, churning out the barges that keep the Reikland's trade afloat.

wiki.title: Kemperbad
wiki.description: Kemperbad, formally the Grand Freistadt of Kemperbad, is an Imperial town within the province of Reikland, said to make the finest brandy in the Empire, while holding freistadt (free city) status.

wiki.title: Rottfurt
wiki.description: Scores of settlements line the River Teufel, most easily forgettable, even interchangeable. Not so Rottfurt, whose name is spoken of in hushed, reverential tones by scholars and wizards throughout the Empire. Though primarily a village of shepherds, producing wool and mutton, Rottfurt also produces a famous — and famously pricy — sheepskin parchment: Rottfurt Silver.

wiki.title: Wittgendorf
wiki.description: Map of the village of Wittgendorf Wittgendorf is an Imperial village located in the Reikland that lies on the west bank of the River Reik, about a mile from Castle Wittgenstein. It was once thriving, but the arrival of the warpstone -spawned "warp storm" that rained down upon the castle as a result of the foul experiments of its ruling Lady Magritte brought a dramatic decline in its fortunes.

properties.name: Hopfberg
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Starter Set - Guide to Ubersreik

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Starter Set - Guide to Ubersreik

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Starter Set - Guide to Ubersreik

wiki.title: Bögenhafen
wiki.description: Bögenhafen is an Imperial town of the Reikland that is a prosperous market centre with a population of roughly 5,000. It sits astride the River Bögen, at the highest point of the river that is still navigable by large sailing vessels. It is also about midway between Altdorf and Montfort on the Axe Bite Pass trade route.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Enemy in Shadows

wiki.title: Wheburg
wiki.description: Wheburg is a resort town in Reikland near Helmgart. It sits on the road from Bögenhafen through Helmgart and over Axe Bite Pass. Because of its proximity to that treacherous road, most people travelling through Wheburg are either about to embark on a potentially fatal journey, or have recently completed one.

properties.name: Zockern
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Enemy in Shadows

wiki.title: Helmgart
wiki.description: Helmgart is an Imperial fortress and market town nestled in the Grey Mountains. It guards the Bretonnian border at Axe Bite Pass. The fortress of Helmgart consists of three great sets of curtain walls, carved directly out of the granite mountainside.

wiki.title: Zahnstadt
wiki.description: Zahnstadt is an isolated village in western Reikland. It is located deep in a high-walled valley, where the rolling hills of the Vorbergland give way to the mighty Grey Mountains. Zahnstadt is notable for the fact that, because of the high craggy valley walls on either side of the village, it receives only a few hours of sunlight in the summer and none at all in the winter.

wiki.title: Hallt
wiki.description: Hallt is an isolated Imperial town located at the foot of the Grey Mountains that is famed for its high walls. It is being harassed by a mutant called the " Headless Horseman of Hallt " on the ominous eve of Hexenstag.

wiki.title: Eilhart
wiki.description: Eilhart is an Imperial town of the Reikland celebrated for the quality of the wines and other alcoholic beverages its people produce. Known and celebrated by wine drinkers throughout the Old World, the vineyards around Eilhart produce the succulent grapes, and thus the wine, that shares its name. Eilhart is widely considered one of the Reikland's best white wines, valued not just for its crisp, light flavour, but also for its famously mild hangovers that grow no worse no matter how much of it was quaffed the night before, or so Eilharters claim.

wiki.title: Schädelheim
wiki.description: Schädelheim is a town in western Reikland, where the River Mos flows into the River Reik. Because of its location on the trade route between Altdorf and Marienburg, it includes many berths for boats and inns for traders. It is also a market town for many settlements throughout the nearby Grootscher Marsh, and ferries run across both the Mos and Reik at Schädelheim.

wiki.title: Holthusen
wiki.description: Holthusen, sometimes spelled Holthausen, is a town in western Reikland. Holthusen is located on the River Schilder, along the primary trade route between the wine -production center of Eilhart and the major trade city of Marienburg. Holthusen's best known export are its barrels, such as the Holthusen Hogshead.

wiki.title: Schilderheim
wiki.description: Schilderheim is an important market town in Reikland, located at the confluence of the River Reik and the River Schilder. Schilderneheim is currently suffering a bout of urban unrest. Although it is one of the Reikland's most important centers of trade, Schilderheim's ambitious burghers look upon the metropoles of Altdorf and Marienburg with envy.

wiki.title: Wörlin
wiki.description: Wörlin is a village along the River Reik in Reikland. Travelling down the river, it would be easy to miss the hamlet, which is nestled between rocky islets and promontories and sheltered by numerous willow trees.

properties.name: Pankenlich
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Enemy in Shadows

wiki.title: Bögensee
wiki.description: High up in the Grey Mountains, the residents of Bögensee are isolated from the rest of the Reikland, close to the eerie ruins of Castle Drachenfels and the haunted stretches of the Grey Lady Pass. Sorrow and death are constant companions to those that live there.

wiki.title: Drakenburg
wiki.description: The town of Drakenburg was a small community deep within the province of Middenland in the dense woods of the Drakwald Forest. The simple life of the villagers was shattered on the day a one-eyed Bonegrinder Giant, known by locals as the Drakwald Cyclops, emerged from the forest and destroyed the town. The only survivor of the massacre was the huntsman Markus Wulfhart, who hunted down and killed the beast in vengeance.

wiki.title: Stromdorf
wiki.description: Stromdorf is a market town in Reikland. It is best known for having an excessively rainy climate. Stromdorf is located on the southern edge of the Reikwald, near the confluence of the Teufel, Ober, and Tranig rivers, which flow out of the Grey Mountains towards the Reik.

wiki.title: Auerswald
wiki.description: The lively town of Auerswald rises by the confluences of the Teufel, Tranig, and Ober rivers, so is on one of the busiest — and thus best patrolled — trade routes of the Reikland. The folk of Auerswald tend to be strong willed and determined, but their easy charm and famous wit ensures no matter how steely their negotiations, they rarely cause offence.

wiki.title: Tallerhof
wiki.description: Tallerhof is an Imperial village of about two hundred dwellings perched on the banks of the River Teufel where the Grey Lady Road meets the Dwarf road in the Teufeltal valley. It is an austere-looking place of windswept, low buildings and grey slate roofs, surrounded by a grey stone wall. Its only notable feature is an ancient iron bridge, built by the Dwarfs long ago for their trade route to the Reikland.

wiki.description: Stimmigen is a market town in the Suden Vorbergland of Reikland. Located on the River Ober near the Vorbergland Canals, many barges bound for Ubersreik pass through Stimmigen. Stimmigen is known for the Ernwald, a variety of apple well-known in Reikland.

wiki.title: Dunkelberg
wiki.description: Dunkelberg, sometimes spelled as Dunkelburg, is a town on the northern bank of the River Grissen. Southernmost of the Reikland's major trade centres, the market town stretches across several hills along the banks of the River Grissen. The older, richer portions of the town sit high on the hills, giving the nobles, and the rising merchant class wealthy enough to afford the oldest townhouses, a commanding view of the surrounding countryside.

properties.name: Dunkelgard
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Starter Set - Guide to Ubersreik

wiki.title: Grissenwald
wiki.description: Grissenwald is a large town in Reikland, with a large Dwarf shantytown known as Khazid Slumbol at it's south wall. Located at the confluence of the Rivers Grissen and Reik. It is a favourite stopping place for riverfolk and boasts a number of wharfside inns.

wiki.title: Diesdorf
wiki.description: Diesdorf is a small town in Reikland, located between Altdorf and Nuln on the River Reik. Corn is the basis of the economy of Diesdorf and its surrounding villages. The crop is mainly traded downriver to Altdorf.

wiki.title: Weissbruck
wiki.description: Weissbruck is a small Imperial town in the Reikland. Located where the Weissbruck Canal to Altdorf meets the River Bögen, it is an important trade centre in the region. Weissbruck originated as a minor fishing village.

history.ruler_2515: Emperor Karl Franz I Holswig Schliestein

wiki.title: Altdorf
wiki.description: Altdorf, known as the " City of Spires," is the current capital city of the Empire of Man, the capital of the Electoral Province of Reikland and an independent Imperial principality in its own right. As the seat of Emperor Karl Franz, Altdorf is the de facto capital of the Empire, and it has been the de jure Imperial capital since the election of Wilhelm III, Prince of Altdorf, to the Imperial throne almost a hundred years ago in 2429 IC.

wiki.title: Gluckshalt
wiki.description: Gluckshalt is an Imperial village not far from Altdorf. Its only point of interest is the temple, which is a large structure, built in the opulent style popular a couple of centuries ago. It is the style of the architects who fled north from the inquisitions in Tilea, who had brought their wide aisles and open colonnades with them.

wiki.title: Frederheim
wiki.description: Frederheim is a small Imperial village situated in the Reikland. Situated just off the Altdorf to Middenheim road, Frederheim is technically a possession of the Emperor, but he has given oversight of it in all but name to the Cult of Shallya, which maintains a walled hospice and sanatorium for the treatment of the insane there. Frederheim is itself a small village with no resources other than farming, and the villagers make ends meet by working for the Sisters.

wiki.title: Balthasar Gelt
wiki.description: Balthasar Gelt, called the " Arch-alchemist ", is the current supreme patriarch of the Imperial Colleges of Magic and one of the Empire 's greatest wizards of the age. The position of supreme patriarch is the highest attainable position by a wizard within the Empire. The supreme patriarch is responsible for advising Emperor Karl Franz in all decisions dealing with the arcane.

wiki.title: Bechafen
wiki.description: Bechafen is a compact city crowded behind its defensive walls and situated on the south bank of the Upper Talabec in the Imperial Electoral Province of Ostermark. Its buildings are narrow and tall, and lean at dizzying angles over alleys that are more like darkened tunnels. Built from the dark wood of the Great Forest, Bechafen’s structures have a gloomy look that no amount of whitewash and coloured trim can dispel.

wiki.title: Fortenhaf
wiki.description: An isolated outpost in the northeast of the province, Fortenhaf is important for its ferry, the largest over the Upper Talabec outside of Bechafen itself. Ruled by the Margrave Konrad Röntgen, Fortenhaf's fortress is an important point for defending Ostermark against invasion, while it also ensures that the proper revenues are collected from any cross-border traffic.

wiki.title: Essen
wiki.description: An isolated town along the North Stir, Essen sits in an unenviable place between the portion of the Great Forest known as the Dead Wood on the west, the Eerie Downs on the East, and the Hel Fenn across the river to the south. Under the rule of the Margrave Gotthold Schurz, Essen has the reputation as the most haunted village in the Empire. Tavern tales say that Ghosts are as common on the streets as people, that Zombies till the fields, and Sylvanian Vampires hunt openly in Essen.

wiki.title: Heffengen
wiki.description: Dead in the centre of Ostermark, Heffengen is ruled by Margrave Richard Dornier, one of the largest breeders of horses in the province. Situated on the edge of the Bleak Moors, Heffengen looks towards the Veldt for its wealth, with the village services dedicated mostly to the summer horse market, which attracts buyers from as far away as Estalia.

wiki.title: Wurzen
wiki.description: In the far south of Ostland on the banks of the Talabec, Wurzen sits almost undisturbed by the events that have ravaged Ostland. True, over a thousand refugees have swelled its population, but the Baron von Wallenstein showed great organisational ability in settling them and arranging for food, shelter, and sanitation. It seemed almost a miracle when the Slaaneshi army that sacked Boven bypassed Wurzen on the way to Zundap, a testament to the Baron's skills at deception and misdirection.

wiki.title: Ferlangen
wiki.description: Ferlangen is an Imperial town that serves as the northern gateway to the Middle Mountains. It is a prosperous town of Ostland that grew out of a fur-trading and timber-felling settlement. Ferlangen's hunters are both accomplished woodsmen and mountain climbers.

wiki.title: Salkalten
wiki.description: Salkalten is an Imperial port town in Ostland that was one of two towns founded as part of a failed attempt to draw trade away from Marienburg (the other being Neues Emskrank in Nordland ). Anyone walking through the town will spy crumbling architectural façades, corroded statues, and other signs of faded glory which, in truth, never really existed.

wiki.title: Schönfeld
wiki.description: Schönfeld is a small, coastal Imperial village located in Ostland. The Skeer, a collection of jagged rocks cutting through the waves west of Salkalten, has claimed many ships. Treacherous currents mean even sailors familiar with the waters spit overboard for Manann 's blessing as they approach.

wiki.title: Bohsenfels
wiki.description: Bohsenfels, also known as " Little Middenheim," is an Imperial fortress-city located in the outer march of Ostland. It is built upon large rocks with caves and tunnels dug underneath, forming a subterranean labyrinth that allows the fortress to maintain enough supplies to hold out against a long siege.

wiki.title: Volganof
wiki.description: Although not nearly as large as Ostland's capital of Wolfenburg, or the coastal city of Salkalten, Volganof is fully enclosed by defensive walls. Indeed, Volganof's soldiers boast their walls are taller and thicker than any others in Ostland and that a foe has never breached them. The formidable city has been built atop a rocky plateau at the junction of the main roadways.

wiki.title: Wolfenburg
wiki.description: Nestled among the foothills of the Middle Mountains, Wolfenburg is the capital city of Ostland in the Empire. It is a beautiful city and the crossroads of trade moving overland between Kislev and the Empire. Its great walls give protection from the things lurking in the Forest of Shadows, and the von Raukovs had brought order and stability to the land after the inept rule of the von Tassenincks.

wiki.description: Stuttburg a harbour town in the Empire. As it borders the sea, it is most likely of the province of Nordland or Ostland.

wiki.description: Map of Nordland; Hargendorf is located west of Dietershafen, along the coast. Hargendorf is a sizable fishing town of Nordland in the Empire, located west of the port city of Dietershafen. It is the home of the Imperial Navy's Second Fleet.

wiki.title: Dunkelkiefer
wiki.description: Dunkelkiefer is a small, isolated settlement of Nordland located near Wrecker's Point. The Jutone Riding is the westernmost county of Nordland, encompassing the remote, desolate headland known colloquially as "Wrecker's Point." The isolated region consists of small hamlets, scattered farmsteads, and a few wretched fishing villages. Foremost amongst these pitiful settlements is Dunkelkiefer, where there is a market, a wooden fort, and very little else.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Salzenmund - City of Salt and Silver

wiki.title: Schuten
wiki.description: Located between Beeckerhoven and Norden on the road to Erengrad, Schuten is a popular stop both with travellers looking to rest for the night and with hunters in need of a base for their forays into the Bramble Hills to the south. It is home to the Brombeerstrauch Inn, a fortified coaching inn owned by a peglegged Dwarf ex-mercenary, Augustus Hargrimsson. Hargrimsson was granted a lifetime concession to run the inn for saving the life of the local baron, Helmuth Adenauer, from a Wyvern, a fight that cost the Dwarf his leg.

wiki.title: Dietershafen
wiki.description: Dietershafen is a coastal city in Nordland and current seat of the Second Fleet of the Imperial Navy. Dietershafen is the Empire 's most important coastal seaport. Its shipyards bustle with activity as shipwrights build new vessels for the Second Fleet.

wiki.title: Neues Emskrank
wiki.description: Neues Emskrank is a miserable Imperial town that skulks at the mouth of the River Salz in Nordland, the legacy of a disastrous mercantile enterprise, that is shunned and avoided by most sensible travellers. Neues Emskrank was the first port in Nordland to open in 2460 IC as a scheme to siphon off business from Marienburg, which failed miserably. The town is now in a permanent state of decline.

wiki.title: Norden
wiki.description: Located at the eastern extreme of the Drosselspule Bay, Nordland, in truth Norden is secretly being developed as base of operations for exploration and conquest of Lustria. It is also used in transporting prisoners to Leopoldheim in the Southlands.

wiki.title: Salzenmund
wiki.description: Salzenmund, the capital city of the Imperial Electoral Province of Nordland and a principality of the Empire in its own right, rests among hills from which flow the tributaries that join to form the River Salz, from which the city gets its name. The Elector Counts built tall castles at the top of these hills overlooking the growing city, once the meeting place for the western scions of the Was Jutone tribe. So narrow is the approach to the keep named the Jutone's Nest that it needs no surrounding curtain wall: the great keep just sits there, watching over the region.

properties.name: Hohenaspe

properties.name: Jutonsryk
properties.source: Time of Legends: God-King (Novel) by Graham McNeill

wiki.title: Jutonsryk
wiki.description: Jutonsryk was an Imperial city of the Wasteland originally founded by the Jutones tribe that stood during the reign of Emperor Sigmar. After the assault of the Liche Nagash on the early Empire and his defeat by the first emperor, Jutonsryk was reduced to a city of the dead, its streets empty of life and infested with degenerate cannibal creatures. "Jutonsryk" was also the name given by King Marius, the founder of the city of Marienburg in the Wasteland, to the entirety of the realm of his Jutones tribe, as it literally meant "Realm of the Jutones."

wiki.title: Sauerapfel
wiki.description: Near where the Aver enters Averland sits the village of Sauerapfel, so named for its famous apple groves, which stretch for miles and miles around the village on both sides of the river. Sauerapfel has close relations with Halstedt, the nearest Stirlander town and its primary market. It also enjoys the revenues from its small port, which handles riverboat traffic entering and leaving the Moot.

wiki.title: Eicheschatten
wiki.description: Eicheschatten, the capital of the Mootland is utterly unprepossessing at first glance. After a longer examination, one’s opinion is confirmed. Home to the Elder of the Mootland, which is the title preferred by Halflings as “Grand Count” sounds “too posh,” Eicheschatten is a collection of winding lanes along the banks of the Aver Reach at the end of the road from Wördern and Halstedt.

properties.name: Hornsby's Ferry
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

properties.name: Leedleton
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Gipfel
wiki.description: A small village in the heart of the Greenleaf Hills, Gipfel is the centre of tobacco production in the Mootland. There are only a few buildings in town, such as a blacksmith and farrier’s shop, communal warehouses, a small temple to Sigmar and all the Halfling gods, and houses for the nearby farms. An inn called The Three Smoke Rings doubles as the meeting place for the village assembly, which is open to all adults.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

properties.name: Bogglewort
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Carroburg
wiki.description: Carroburg is a small Imperial city that once served as the capital of the former Electoral Province of Drakwald before its formal dissolution in 1124 IC, after which time it became a part of Middenland. Carroburg's economy specializes in trade and the manufacture of glass, and pottery, with its present day ruler being Duke Leopold von Bildhofen.

properties.name: Koldust
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Realm of the Ice Queen

wiki.title: Grimmenhagen
wiki.description: Grimmenhagen is a walled town, its people were accustomed to fighting Beastmen, and over the last few centuries, it had been destroyed and rebuilt many times, each incorporating the ruins of the old to buttress new fortifications to stave off their attackers. In its most recent incarnation, a high wall with towers encircled the place, making it a powerful stronghold to fight against Chaos. Famed for its halberdiers, these troops split their time defending the town and the nearby Sternhauer Keep —the ancestral home of the town's ruler, Graf Elster Sternhauer.

wiki.title: Untergard
wiki.description: Untergard is a young town, founded only a century ago by villagers fleeing the unjust taxes of Graf Sternhauer. They built a bridge across the Taub and soon the town straddled both sides of the river. As the only crossing place south of Grimminhagen, it was a natural target for Archaon's forces and a fierce battle was fought there.

properties.name: Magnusdorf
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Battles 6th Edition: The Nemesis Crown

wiki.title: Delberz
wiki.description: Delberz is an important Imperial town and port on the Middenheim-Altdorf Road in Middenland. Situated on the River Delb along the Middenheim-Altdorf Road, Delberz is a prosperous mercantile community well known for the quality of its local wines. Several inns dot the town; some have large stables attached that cater to caravans, while others by the docks offer warehousing services as a sideline.

Lindenheim is an Imperial village in Middenland that is a community of foresters and smallholders, centred on the Lindenheim Trading Post, a hub for the region's merchants, farmers, foresters, and trappers to do business.

wiki.title: Hovelhof
wiki.description: A map of Middenheim; Hovelhof lies in the centre of the province. Hovelhof is a small impoverished Imperial village, perched atop a high hill with spectacular views eastward to the mountains and southward to Middenheim. The air is sweet and clear, the upland meadows lush, and the sky is a vibrant, cloudless blue.

wiki.title: Middenheim
wiki.description: Middenheim, also known as the Ulricsberg, the Fauschlag (meaning "Fist-Strike" in Reikspiel ), or simply the " City of the White Wolf," is amongst the greatest and most fortified fortress-cities within the Old World and beyond. Middenheim is home to the Cult of Ulric and is the greatest city-state of the northern Empire, as well as the capital of the Grand Province of Middenland. The City of the White Wolf is the rock upon which the northern enemies of the Empire have always broken upon.

wiki.title: Schattenlas
wiki.description: Schattenlas is an Imperial village of the Middenland that is little more than a dozen family farmhouses and a granary, built atop a rare patch of high ground protected from flooding. Wood rots fast this close to the Furdienst, so the buildings are raised on stone foundations, and their roofs thatched with reeds. At the base of the hill, 80 yards from the village, a community jetty affixes a couple of fishing boats, and a ferry that helps travellers cross the Furdienst for a fee.

wiki.title: Middenstag
wiki.description: This forbidding castle, known as the Middenstag, rises up out of the outskirts of the Drakwald. A key garrison of the Knights Panther, those posted here protect the main route from Hochland to Delberz and who patrol the Howling Hills, an area noted for danger.

properties.name: Gladbeich
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Power Behind the Throne Companion

wiki.title: Gladbeich
wiki.description: A traveller approaches the village of Gladbeich. Gladbeich is a sleepy little Imperial village located several days' journey east of Middenheim, in the Barony of Holzbek along the Kleiflusch River. Lately, dreadful cries are reported to shake the very stones of the nearby Middle Mountains at all hours.

wiki.title: Hergig
wiki.description: The capital of Hochland, Hergig is home to the Ludenhof family and was once the site of a mighty fortress, originally with a population of 9,200. Hergig was also home to the Hochland College of Sorcery, a school licensed by the Emperor for the academic study of magic and its theory. With quarries nearby, the town before the Storm of Chaos was rebuilding itself as a modern place of stone and brick, its small Dwarf Quarter supplying their skills in the construction.

properties.name: Bergsburg
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Archives of the Empire 1

wiki.title: Gruyden
wiki.description: Gruyden is a small Imperial Shrine Village that is located just a hundred miles south-west from the capital of Hochland, Hergig. Ruled by the famously devout Auerbach family, the village of Gruyden sits along a branch of roads off the New Road to Hergig. Interspersed among the homes and cottages of the population are amazing shrines to all the major gods of the Empire, with those of Sigmar, Taal and Rhya being the largest.

wiki.title: Esk
wiki.description: Esk is a small mining and logging town in Hochland, most noted for its nearby copper mines. Raw ore was smelted into ingots and then shipped down river to Bergendorf for further distribution, as that route was often safer than the shorter road. The nearby castle was home to the bailiff of Esk, a retainer of Elector Count Aldebrand Ludenhof.

wiki.title: Bergendorf
wiki.description: Bergendorf was a village sacked in 2522 IC, its population of 93 still missing.

wiki.title: Valnein
wiki.description: Valnein was a sleepy village nestled deep within the Empire. Once devoted to Sigmar, its inhabitants eventually fell under the sway of Tzeentch, the Chaos God of change and intrigue. The village was later reduced to ash by its own priest of Sigmar.

wiki.title: Averheim
wiki.description: Averheim is the capital city of the Grand Province of Averland, and the original capital of the ancient Brigundians tribe. Averheim has been the chief city of the land between the river Aver and the river Reik since before the legendary Emperor Sigmar was born. It sits on a bluff above the river Aver, and so is immune from its occasional high floods.

wiki.title: Streissen
wiki.description: Streissen is a town in Averland that harbors a ferry system, and a history of volatile conspiracy. If the spirit of revolution has taken hold among the usually traditional Averlanders, it is in the town of Streissen. A town with a small university and medical school, Streissen has always been ready to take in new ideas from elsewhere, such that Averlanders often refer to someone from Streissen as “not quite right in the head,” or “too much under the influence of Nulners and Stirlanders.” Streissen’s middle and upper classes take pride in their relative openness to new ideas and think of themselves as Averland’s intellectual elite.

wiki.title: Grenzstadt
wiki.description: Grenzstadt is an Imperial fortress-town that is located at the northwestern end of Black Fire Pass, and commands lucrative trade traffic from traders moving through the Old Dwarf Road. Ruled by a representative of the Elector Count, Grenzstadt is a centre of the fur, gem, and metal trade, with a large guild market and warehouses within its walls. At any given time, foreign merchants, trade caravans, and pilgrims can all be seen in the town.

wiki.title: Heideck
wiki.description: Heideck is an Imperial town located at the crossroads of the Old Dwarf Road just before reaching the capital of Averheim. Built as a way station at the height of the Dwarf Empire, Heideck was in ruins when humans first occupied the area in the first millenium. It has since become an important crossroad for traffic from the Upper Reik via Agbeiten and from Black Fire Pass to Averheim and vice versa.
